meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You will handle general supervision.
You look simply like a princess.
Just do not scare me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'look'.

examples.trans: The costume looks simply super!
On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You look simply like a princess.

examples.text: Я пришёл попросить у тебя прощения.
examples.trans: I came to ask your forgiveness.
Chef, forgive me for the dish.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You look simply like a princess.
Denis, how did you get in here?
Let us do it like in the old days!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нцесса'). Common feminine noun meaning 'princess' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You look simply like a princess.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть принцесса.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always princess.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: С возвращением тебя к нам, Витя!
examples.trans: Welcome back to us, Vitya!
Misha, thank you for everything.
And thank you all very much.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'prince' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He brought his own team here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: But a special thank you to my son-in-law.
That title will be his in twenty-four hours.
Let us go to the kitchen quickly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.trans: And you have an excellent prince.
That is simply a great plan!
It'll be an excellent flat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Misha, thank you for everything.

examples.text: Всю жизнь я за тебя боялась.
examples.trans: All my life I was afraid for you.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be afraid (of), to fear'.

related.gloss: not to to be afraid (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.
I'm not afraid.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Only the best work in the kitchen!
Just do not scare me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Папа, он пока ещё не зять.
examples.trans: Dad, he is not your son-in-law yet.
Vitya, you must not get nervous at all.
I actually like this idea.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to scare, frighten', paired with 'испугать'.

examples.trans: Just do not scare me.

examples.text: Первый раз вижу, чтобы людей удочкой пугали.
examples.trans: It's the first time I've seen anyone scare people with a fishing rod.
Don't scare me!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'at least', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Although I am calm about you.
I wanted to talk with you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('calm / at ease').

examples.trans: Although I am calm about you.

examples.text: Слушай, давай спокойно с тобой поговорим.
